clue.text: Officer starts marching, hopeful of meeting someone halfway

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for Commanding Officer

indicators.note: the start of the word marching supplies just its opening letter

parts.note: a hopeful prospect is a promising one

explanation.surface: An officer setting off on a march hopes to strike a deal with someone halfway along.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling a dispute by mutual concession means each side yields ground, the sense of the present participle here.

clue.text: Leave very little time to reduce the sentence

definitions.meaning: to allow only the narrowest margin of time for something
read literally: to trim down a judicial penalty

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to allow a bare minimum of time, while read literally it means shortening a penalty.

clue.text: Planet rising in temperature

definitions.meaning: the innermost planet of the solar system
the liquid metal that climbs a thermometer tube as it gets warmer

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the innermost planet and to the metal used in thermometers that climbs as heat increases.

clue.text: Fault admitted by assistant setting up store

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up turns its letters upward, so they read backwards
the fault is let inside the word for assistant

parts.note: an assistant is a helper
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: An assistant owns up to a mistake made while opening a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses the assembled HSINELPER; 'store' is a verb here, not a shop, despite the retail surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To store something up is to stock or fill again, here as a verb meaning restock.

clue.text: Student leaves titbit for a walrus

indicators.note: the student departs, so that letter is dropped from the titbit word

parts.note: a titbit is a morsel
L, the learner-driver plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student walks away from a tasty snack meant for a walrus.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign displayed by British learner drivers, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic English name for the walrus, from the old northern word for the animal.

clue.text: Nature's variety seen in a leisurely stroll

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

parts.note: the letters of the word, with its S, used as fodder

explanation.surface: Nature's rich diversity can be enjoyed on an unhurried walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges NATURES, the letters of Nature's including the S, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle, unhurried walk is exactly this word, used as a noun.

clue.text: A river once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A river climbs and drops repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: A, R and AGAIN make ARAGAIN; 'rises' turns the whole lot upward, reading NIAGARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border go by this name, so it can stand for the falls themselves.

clue.text: Existing expenses

parts.note: existing is read as staying alive, so these are the outgoings needed simply to live

explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary everyday outgoings for food, housing and bills are what it costs simply to exist.

clue.text: Rock formation cut away at first

indicators.note: the word for away is placed at the front, before the word for cut

parts.note: someone away is out
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A rocky formation is cut back early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological term for rock that protrudes above the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Fool might use this? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a fool is a creamy fruit dessert, often made with this pink-stalked plant
an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish, also the word actors mutter for crowd noise

explanation.surface: A silly person might resort to talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool here is the British pudding of stewed fruit folded into cream, not a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The stalk vegetable makes a classic fruit fool, and the same word is slang for meaningless talk.

clue.text: Bred in sin, set out this indication of it?

definitions.text: Bred in sin, set out this indication of it?

indicators.note: set out signals that the preceding letters are laid out afresh in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, used as fodder

explanation.surface: Being born out of wedlock is marked by a heraldic sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BRED IN SIN SET are rearranged by 'out'; the whole clue also defines, since this heraldic band traditionally marks illegitimate birth.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry this diagonal band from upper right to lower left was popularly held to denote illegitimacy.

clue.text: Payment subject to approval

parts.note: read one way, a sum paid by a subject people to their ruler; read another, an expression of approval or praise

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both money paid by a subordinate state and a gesture of praise or esteem.

clue.text: Net adjustment by water board

indicators.note: an adjustment to the word net rearranges its letters

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A water authority makes a net change to its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' rearranges NET to ENT, which is followed by RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a railway carriage is to get on a train, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Like whiskey, if rye is used to make it

indicators.note: the letters of if rye are used, rearranged, to make the answer

parts.note: the letters of these two words, as fodder

explanation.surface: Whiskey made from rye has a burning kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to make it' rearranges the five letters of IF RYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong spirits burn the throat, so whiskey is described as hot and burning.

clue.text: There's no end of them in legends

definitions.text: There's no end of them in legends

parts.words: There's no end of them in legends
parts.note: no end of them suggests a great number, but really means beings whose lives never end, the gods and heroes of myth

explanation.definitionFit: Gods and deathless heroes of myth live for ever, so their lives have no end.

clue.text: Thought broadcast item dated

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, as fodder

explanation.surface: A news item that has gone out on air is now old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the nine letters of ITEM DATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pondered or reflected deeply is to have thought, past tense in both.

clue.text: Attacked and beaten, he'd give in

indicators.note: beaten eggs are whisked up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored, as fodder

explanation.surface: Having been assaulted and defeated, he says he would surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges HEDGIVEIN, the letters of he'd give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To have railed or protested bitterly against something is to have attacked it in words.

clue.text: House accommodating an orchid

indicators.note: the house takes the next word in as a guest, putting it inside

parts.note: a villa is a house

explanation.surface: A house is home to an orchid.
explanation.definitionFit: The flavouring comes from the pods of a climbing tropical orchid, which shares the name.

clue.text: Multiply without going forth

parts.note: multiply is to reproduce, and doing so without going out means mating within the family

explanation.definitionFit: Mating closely related stock means reproducing within the group rather than outside it.

clue.text: More than one ghost writer

parts.note: a ghost writer suggests someone writing for another, but this is the author of the play Ghosts

explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist wrote the play called Ghosts, so he wrote more than one ghost.

clue.text: I'm old-fashioned, there's no getting away from it

definitions.text: there's no getting away from it

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
passe means out of date

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being behind the times and unable to escape it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation with no way out, a dead end.

clue.text: It may help to preserve the ocean sailor

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman might help keep the ocean safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt evaporated from seawater is used for curing and preserving food.

clue.text: Base for soldier in retreat, one of rank

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the soldier word reads in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a noble is a person of high rank

explanation.surface: A soldier on the retreat is sent back to base by a ranking officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of low, dishonourable or mean in character.

clue.text: Run out of paintings for mounting

parts.note: ex means out of, from

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the letters climb, reading upwards

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of pictures to frame.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run not scored off the bat (a bye, wide or no-ball) is called an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a run credited to the batting side that was not hit off the bat.

clue.text: They're associated with heads and tails

definitions.text: They're associated with heads and tails

parts.words: They're associated with heads and tails
parts.note: heads and tails suggests a coin toss, but means tall hats worn on the head with tailcoats in formal dress

explanation.definitionFit: Tall silk hats are worn on the head as part of formal morning dress with a tailcoat.

clue.text: Librettist bound to accept pound note

indicators.note: the bound word takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: girt means bound or encircled
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A lyric writer is obliged to take a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the libretti, the words, for the Savoy operas set to Sullivan's music.

clue.text: Note to say one is willing

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A written note declares that someone is prepared to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' here means having made a will, not being keen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid will is described as testate, punning on willing.

clue.text: Extremely important body parts

parts.note: extremely suggests very, but points to the extremities of the body, the parts at its far ends

explanation.definitionFit: The extremities of the limbs are the parts of the body furthest from its centre.
